name: Underdog
label: Revelation
lede: Two skaters met at CBGB, built a hardcore band that could sing, handed a guitar to the first Black skater on a Thrasher cover, and called it quits the minute the van got home.

eras.title: Two skaters meet at CBGB
eras.text: Richie Birkenhead had just come out of the Numskuls and Russ Iglay had just walked away from Murphy's Law. They met at CBGB and started a band that wanted hardcore's speed with actual melody on top, and a skate ramp somewhere in the background.

years.src: Double Cross: Russ Iglay · Bridge Nine · Ice and I
years.h: Richie Birkenhead and Russ Iglay start Underdog
years.p: Richie Birkenhead (vocals) and Russ "Wheeler" Iglay (bass) meet at CBGB and decide to start a band. Danny Derella plays guitar and Greg Pierce drums.
years.xp:
Russ Iglay says Underdog came together about a week after he left [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]]. Birkenhead had been fronting the Numskuls since 1983.

Both were serious skaters. Birkenhead has named Tony Alva, Duane Peters and Neil Blender as heroes right alongside [[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]], [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and SSD.

years.h: Underdog's True Blue demo at Electric Reels
years.p: Richie Birkenhead, Russ Iglay, Danny Derella and Greg Pierce cut eight songs, including True Blue, Say It (To My Face)! and the skate anthem Frontside Grind.

years.h: Richie Birkenhead plays guitar in Youth of Today, then comes back
years.p: Richie Birkenhead spends 1986 on guitar in [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], then leaves Ray Cappo's band to put everything into Underdog.

years.h: Greg Pierce leaves for college; Dean Joseph takes Underdog's drums
years.p: After a few months and a handful of shows, drummer Greg Pierce leaves for college in Florida. Dean Joseph of Good Humor replaces him, playing in both bands until Underdog starts touring.
years.xp: Russ Iglay also remembers a second guitarist, Arthur, who made the band sound bigger but left after an early tour. Iglay's version: Underdog toured loose and Arthur took it seriously, and that didn't mix.

eras.title: Sunday matinees and Jersey Shore Elks halls
eras.text: Underdog became a fixture at the CBGB matinees and down the Jersey Shore, the band that could scream one line and croon the next. Richie Birkenhead's voice, as their booking agent later put it, went from guttural to choirboy mid-song.

years.h: Underdog at the CBGB matinee, April 17, 1988
years.p: A full Underdog set from the Bowery, filmed and passed around on tape for decades, with Richie Birkenhead and Russ Iglay at the front of the stage.

years.h: Underdog at the Belmar Elks Club, New Jersey
years.p: Russ Iglay says Underdog's mid-1988 show at the Belmar Elks Club was the one Jersey Shore kids kept bringing up for years. City Gardens in Trenton and the Stone Pony in Asbury Park became regular stops too.

years.h: Underdog's Over the Edge demo at Don Fury's
years.p: Seven songs cut at Don Fury's studio in Manhattan, among them Over the Edge, Mass Movement and The Vanishing Point. The tape gets Underdog signed to Caroline Records.

eras.title: A pro skater on guitar, then home for good
eras.text: Underdog finally made an album, with a Thrasher cover star playing guitar, and took it across the country. It was the peak, and it was the end.

years.src: Double Cross: Russ Iglay · Wikipedia: Chuck Treece
years.h: Pro skater Chuck Treece joins Underdog on guitar
years.p: Pro skater Tom Groholski introduces Underdog to [[Chuck Treece|ef661f53-d4b4-4903-811c-f3dcb1b970f3]], the Philadelphia skater and [[McRad|df55082c-8a17-448d-a9c9-e3c7f00546a7]] leader. Treece, the first African-American skater on a Thrasher cover (1984), completes the classic lineup.
years.xp: Treece was a sponsored pro from 1982 to 1990, riding for Santa Cruz, Powell-Peralta and Airwalk, and he'd go on to play with [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]]. With Richie Birkenhead, Russ Iglay and Dean Joseph, he's the lineup most fans mean when they say Underdog.

years.h: Underdog land on Thrasher's Skate Rock Volume 7
years.p: Russ Iglay says Pushead picked Underdog for the cassette-only Skate Rock series from Thrasher magazine, the skate world's own mixtape.

q: Underdog always existed on the fringes.
years.h: The Vanishing Point, Underdog's only album · Caroline
years.p: Eleven songs for Caroline Records, produced by Don Fury, mixing hardcore with melody and even reggae. Most of it is the Over the Edge demo songs, rebuilt with Chuck Treece on guitar.
years.xp:
Caroline pressed it on LP, CD and cassette in the US, with a Belgian CD for Europe. Tracks include Over the Edge, Back to Back, Blindside and the title track.

Richie Birkenhead never loved the hardcore tag. Underdog, he told Noisecreep, always sat on the edges of it.

q: Once we came home from that tour, that was pretty much the end
years.src: Double Cross: Russ Iglay · Finding Connecticut
years.h: Underdog's Vanishing Point tour, and the end of the band
years.p: Underdog take The Vanishing Point on a national tour, their best run ever. Russ Iglay says that once the van got back to New York, Underdog was done.
years.xp: There was no big blowup on the record. The tour went well, the band went on hiatus, and the hiatus turned permanent. Richie Birkenhead was already writing songs that didn't fit hardcore at all.

eras.title: Into Another, and the tapes on Revelation
eras.text: Richie Birkenhead went somewhere much stranger with Into Another. Meanwhile Revelation, the label run by his old Youth of Today circle, put both Underdog demos on one record.

years.src: Ice and I · Wikipedia: Richie Birkenhead
years.h: Richie Birkenhead forms Into Another
years.p: Richie Birkenhead starts [[Into Another|c235e5fd-4144-4e53-95ff-b33dc5f239c8]] with Drew Thomas of [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]]. They sign to Revelation and later to Hollywood Records.
years.xp: Birkenhead's explanation for moving on from Underdog was stagnation, not boredom: he felt he couldn't express himself fully in the old band.

years.h: Underdog's Demos LP · Revelation REV 28
years.p: Revelation puts the December 1985 True Blue demo on side A and the fall 1988 Over the Edge demo on side B. First press: 1,900 black and 300 blue.

eras.title: Back for benefits, Japan and CBGB's last stand
eras.text: A reissue brought Underdog back in 1998, and after that the band came out whenever something mattered: a benefit, a festival, the fight to save CBGB. The classic core, Richie Birkenhead, Russ Iglay and Dean Joseph, kept showing up.

years.h: Go-Kart Records reissues The Vanishing Point
years.p: Go-Kart puts Underdog's album back out on LP, red vinyl and CD, with live bonus tracks on the CD.

years.h: Underdog reunite at Asbury Park's Convention Hall
years.p: Underdog play the Alive and Well benefit at Convention Hall in Asbury Park, then tour for Go-Kart with Jay from American Standard on drums and Matt Dolan on guitar.

years.h: Underdog play benefits to save CBGB
years.p: Underdog's original core plays benefit shows for CBGB, first with [[Killing Time|9e3c100d-51c9-43da-b21d-4dcead9a3142]]. Russ Iglay says later dates put them on bills with [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] and the Stimulators.

years.h: Underdog play the Magma Festival in Japan
years.p: Eighteen years after The Vanishing Point, Underdog fly to Japan for the Magma Festival.

years.h: Underdog at the Burning Fight Festival, Chicago
years.p: Underdog join the reunion-heavy Burning Fight Festival in Chicago.

eras.title: Matchless, sober, and nine kids later
eras.text: Underdog never made new music and never pretended they would. They collected the old songs on Bridge Nine and kept playing them, with a Floorpunch guitarist filling out the classic lineup.

years.src: Double Cross: Russ Iglay · Revelation Records
years.h: Matchless: every Underdog song on Bridge Nine
years.p: Bridge Nine (B9R133) puts The Vanishing Point and the demos together, 26 tracks, as a gatefold double LP and CD.
years.xp:
Russ Iglay says talks with Revelation were moving slowly, so he emailed Bridge Nine's Chris Wrenn, who answered within hours. Iglay liked the label's hard deadlines.

Iglay also credited his own sobriety for how well Underdog was going. New songs? The band's nine kids made that close to impossible, he said, and Underdog wouldn't want it any other way.

years.h: Underdog at Space Ballroom, Hamden, Connecticut
years.p: Richie Birkenhead, Russ Iglay and Dean Joseph, with Marc "Zev" Zeveney of [[Floorpunch|8ecf80c2-d090-4cbd-97ec-0a0824301041]] on guitar, play an all-ages show at Space Ballroom.
